Archie vs hiring an assistant.

These are not the same purchase, and anyone telling you a piece of software replaces a person is selling you something. What follows is where each one is actually the right call.

Archie is in testing. The waitlist hears the day it opens. See where it stands → Checked against the sources below on August 19, 2026.

The short answer

A person handles judgement. An agent handles repetition.

Almost every job people hand an assistant is a mix of the two, and the mix decides this. Chasing replies, moving meetings and assembling the same summary every Monday is repetition, and it can be handed to software. Deciding what matters, speaking on your behalf, and knowing when the rule should be broken is a person’s work, and it stays one.

Where an agent wins

Four things an agent does that no person will.

A person handles the calls only a person can make. These are the other hours of the week.

An agent costs $30 a month, plus AI at cost

$1 to $5 a month of AI for a handful of tasks a day, on your own account, with a cap you setSource 1.

An agent is up before you are, and on Sunday

A brief before six, an inbox watched through the weekend, the same list kept every day.

An agent never tires of the same task

Repetition is what it is for, and the hundredth time is done like the first.

An agent asks before it acts, in code

A mistake waits for your yes rather than going out under your nameSource 2.

Side by side

What each one is like to live with.

Archie compared with a part-time assistant, across hours, onboarding, judgement, discretion and cost
  Archie A part-time assistant
Hours Whenever the computer is on, including six in the morning The hours you agreed, minus holiday and sick leave
Getting it up to speed You write down how you like things once, and it is written down Weeks, and it lives in their head
Judgement on something new Drafts, then waits for youSource 2 Decides, and tells you afterwards
Phone calls and difficult people No Yes, and this is often the whole reason to hire one
If they leave Nothing leaves; the instructions are files on your computerSource 3 You start again
Who sees your inbox Software on your own computer, on your own accountsSource 3 Another person, which is a matter of trust rather than of access control
What you pay $30Source 1 a month for the app, plus your own AI usage A wage, plus payroll, plus the time it takes to manage someone

The last row is deliberately unpriced. Assistant pay swings by country, by seniority and by how many hours you want, far more than one figure can carry, and the only rate that matters to you is the one where you are hiring. We would rather leave the cell in words than print a number that is wrong for most of the people reading it.

Where a person wins

Four things no agent does.

None of these is a gap we expect to close, and you should weigh them properly.

A person takes responsibility

A person can be accountable for an outcome. Software cannot, which is exactly why Archie holds every email and calendar change until you approve itSource 2: the responsibility never left you.

A person reads the room

Knowing that this particular client should be called rather than emailed, and that today is not the day to chase the invoice, is not a rule anyone can write down for you.

A person acts in the world

Phone calls, doors, couriers, the awkward conversation. An agent works inside your accounts and nowhere else.

A person notices what you didn’t ask about

A good assistant tells you the thing you would not have thought to look for. An agent does what its routines say and answers what you asked.

Worth saying

If you already have an assistant, this makes their week better.

The repetitive half of the job is the half nobody enjoys. Handing the Monday summary and the reply-chasing to an agent gives the person you hired their attention back for the work you actually hired them for.

Sources for every figure and claim on this page
1Archie, $30 a month

Our own price, with the AI usage that sits on top of it broken down on the pricing page.

2Nothing sends without you

Email and calendar changes are drafted and held for approval in the app. The mechanism, and the honest limit on it, are on the Trust page.

3On your own computer, on your own accounts

Archie runs on your computer and talks to your accounts directly. The Trust page lists every outbound connection it makes and tells you how to watch it yourself with a network monitor.

No wage figure, on purpose

One number would have to cover part-time and full-time, one country and another, a first job and ten years of experience. Any figure we printed would be right for somebody and misleading for everybody else, so this comparison is argued on what the work looks like instead. Your own local rate is the figure to weigh it against.
